event_data.context:
## Workflow contract

For every green implementation increment:

1. Run the repository-owned pre-commit hook as the only synchronous local checkpoint gate.
2. Keep that hook limited to checks that must pass before another iteration may safely begin: focused/fast unit tests, formatting, linting, manifest/config validation, and similarly bounded checks.
3. Create the signed commit and push immediately when pre-commit passes. Do not repeat the same full suite locally before pushing.
4. Begin the next iteration without waiting for pushed CI to finish.
5. Monitor every pushed SHA concurrently. A terminal CI failure immediately preempts feature work and enters the existing Tiber-owned recovery hold; diagnose whether the pushed SHA caused it, then perform one causal repair or an authorized unchanged-SHA rerun.
6. Let CI own comprehensive, slow, integration, mutation, broad acceptance, and other pipeline-scale gates. Avoid running identical comprehensive gates in pre-commit, a second local exact-commit step, and CI.
7. Keep the full multi-lens final review separate: it runs only when the ticket is otherwise ready to be declared done, not before every checkpoint.

## Project setup and portability

Apply this as the default operating procedure for repositories configured by the Development System plugin. Setup and migration guidance must help projects classify checks by latency, causal value, and whether they must block the next edit. Existing repositories need a safe adoption path that does not silently discard project-specific checks.

The policy must compose with direct-to-trunk, pull-request, and local-only delivery modes. Direct-to-trunk pushes after the fast hook. Pull-request mode pushes the authorized branch checkpoint and monitors branch/PR CI without inferring permission to open or merge. Local-only mode records that no push or remote CI is authorized.

## Tests and evals

Add deterministic coverage for gate classification, immediate push, concurrent next-iteration work plus CI monitoring, CI-failure preemption, and non-duplication of comprehensive suites. Add model-mediated fixtures proving the agent does not serialize on successful CI, does not skip monitoring, and does stop new feature work immediately on failure.
event_data.summary: Define and enforce a Development System SOP that keeps the synchronous pre-commit checkpoint gate fast and sufficient for starting the next iteration, pushes immediately after that gate passes, runs comprehensive verification in CI, and monitors CI concurrently so any failure preempts ongoing work through the existing Tiber recovery protocol.
event_data.title: Standardize fast pre-commit checkpoints with asynchronous CI recovery
